wording: - **In scope.** An individual with a residence or habitual abode in Germany, taxed on worldwide income (§ 1(1) EStG), who earns profit from self-employed work (§ 18 EStG, Anlage S) or a trade (§ 15 EStG, Anlage G), and works out profit by the cash method (§ 4(3) EStG). Single or jointly assessed with a spouse.
classification: positive legal/admin rule, actual own-source quotation
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Freiberufler or trade.** Only a trade pays trade tax and gets the § 35 credit. The named professions in § 18(1) no. 1 EStG (doctors, lawyers, engineers, architects, tax advisers, journalists, translators and similar) and scientific, artistic, writing and teaching work are Freiberufler. Everything else run for profit is a trade (§ 15(2) EStG). Unclear cases: refer (see de-einkommensteuer-freelancer).
classification: positive legal/admin rule, actual own-source quotation
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Cash method or books.** A trader must keep books once the tax office gives notice after turnover over EUR 800,000 or trade profit over EUR 80,000 in a year (§ 141 AO). A Freiberufler can always use the cash method. Books are out of scope here.
classification: positive legal/admin rule, actual own-source quotation
disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Who must file.** Without wages, anyone whose total income is above the basic allowance (twice it for spouses) (§ 56 EStDV). With business income the return and the EÜR must be sent electronically (§ 25(4) EStG, § 60(4) EStDV).

disposition: Exact original current unit; only native LF rebound

wording: - **Out of scope.** Companies (GmbH, UG): de-corporate-tax. Partnerships (GbR, OHG, KG, PartG), whose profit is fixed at partnership level. Non-residents with German business income: de-non-resident-tax. Selling or closing the business, extraordinary income (§ 34 EStG), retained profits (§ 34a EStG), foreign income and treaties.

wording:
**Cars.** A car used more than 50% for business can be a business asset: all costs are expenses and private use is added back at 1% of the gross list price per month (§ 6(1) no. 4 EStG), or by logbook. A private car used for business trips: EUR 0.30 per km or the actual cost share. Home-to-premises travel uses the commuting allowance and, for a business car, the additional adjustment below. Electric and hybrid cars have special rules: refer.

**Business-car commuting adjustment, ordinary combustion car.** In addition to the separate private-use add-back, § 4(5) no. 6 EStG disallows `max(0, D − A)` for travel between home and the business premises. Under the list-price method, `D = 0.0003 × domestic list price at first registration × full one-way kilometres × calendar months`. `A` is the statutory commuting allowance: for this ordinary car case, `EUR 0.38 × full one-way kilometres × actual commuting days`, applying the § 9(1) no. 4 distance and benefit-reduction conditions. When private use is valued under § 6(1) no. 4 sentence 1 or 3, including the logbook method, use the actual documented costs of these commuting trips as `D` instead. Electric/hybrid reductions and family-home trips need their separate rules.

For a stipulated ordinary car with a EUR 40,000 list price, 20 full km, 12 months and 200 commuting days, `D = 2,880`, `A = 1,520`, and the extra nondeductible amount is EUR 1,360. With actual/logbook commuting costs of EUR 1,000 the extra amount is zero; with EUR 2,000 it is EUR 480. These amounts are separate from the private-use add-back.
classification: positive legal/admin rule, actual own-source quotation
disposition: Bounded DE-R01–08 wording/evidence successor
